Its veto and its limits

  • Governance: an unrespected binding ExCo veto, an unresolved red-line flag, a withheld or absent CFO co-signature (her veto check not concurring with that value, or a launch or commit added at the revise step that her memo did not co-sign) or an override the team rule does not allow inference RX-0213 R-1579 RG-0044
  • Safety and maturity, judged on the final orders: an unconditional launch or commit that cannot meet the EIS it serves, or an item on which the operating head's binding Civil veto still stands after the revision; never a zero-margin pass, capacity or MRO advice, or a concern the revision cured inference RG-0027 RG-0025 R-1476 RX-0296
  • No airframe on the record for an unconditional launch (alternative: launch if selected or hold) R-0994 R-1005 RX-0058
  • Profit: a narrowbody launch, launch if selected or commit whose weighted value against hold is below 0, or an unconditional Solo below the ExCo's bar inference R-1005 R-1011 R-1582
  • Premium, counted per item: a widebody item's shortfall against its hold row that is undeclared, given for narrowbody share, or above the $3B cap ($1B for an UltraFan WB); a gap from a field held at default is never charged to an item inference R-1574 R-1010
  • Reasonable worst case: an item that can lose more than its own bill in a plausible column inference RG-0033 RG-0031
  • Overlapping programmes: NB Solo beside UltraFan WB unless both are selected, or the upgrade beside an UltraFan in development or ordered launch if selected this round inference R-0929 R-1127 RG-0019 RX-0214
  • Partner alignment: a Joint Venture commit before P&W's commitment is on the record or a live airframe's code includes P&W inference R-1010 R-0318
  • Cancel discipline: the cancel of a programme a live airframe flies inference R-0986 R-1573
  • Balance-sheet weakening: a new unconditional launch or commit while the CFO invokes a balance-sheet veto or an other move needs equity, leverage above about 1.5x or borrowing for distributions; never a fall in the brief's delta PV inference R-0986 R-0053 RG-0031
  • Balance sheet: a plan needing equity, leverage above about 1.5x or borrowing for distributions RG-0041 RX-0261 RX-0215
  • Limits: the veto binds; a vetoed item goes back to the CEO once (board revise), with no override against the board, and after the confirm a still-vetoed item reverts to the default (hold); every veto names acceptable alternatives, values of that field that pass the tests, the default included (only values legal this round); the board never originates orders and never vetoes a hold, an item merely because another plan scores higher (within the $3B cap, $1B for an UltraFan WB, that is the CEO's declared premium), an item for its near-term earnings cost alone, an item on the public statement alone, or an item because the brief's delta PV is below 0 inference RG-0017

Its recommendations

Priority-led and plain, in the chair's register: one absolute priority, then the discipline, then the long-term growth story. Typical asks: an airframe first, through launch if selected; a partner once P&W has committed; the widebody core and durability; the reasonable worst case of every item; no early date; one big programme at a time in a flat R&D envelope; cancel what no airframe can use. The CEO answers each in board response (taken up, or why not); an unanswered one is raised again next round, but is not a veto ground by itself. What the Board holds management to

  1. Product safety and maturity before entry into service: safety always the most important priority; the board oversaw the Trent 1000 crisis; the company left a Boeing engine rather than compress maturity RG-0027 RG-0025 R-1476 R-0970
  2. A strong balance sheet: a strong investment-grade rating, prudent leverage, robust liquidity, no equity raise to rebuild it; single A from Moody's and Fitch since 2026 RX-0242 RG-0041 RG-0043 RX-0261 RX-0215 RG-0060
  3. Financial and operational performance: profit and cash over market share RG-0015 RG-0018 RG-0029 R-1561 R-1582
  4. Shareholder payments from sustainable free cash flow (a 30-40% payout and buybacks), after the cash needs of the business; now £7-9bn of buybacks planned for 2026-2028 R-0738 RG-0028 R-0909 RG-0042 RG-0059
  5. Disciplined investment: an airframe first, profitable or not at all, mid-to-high-teens hurdles, one big programme at a time R-1005 R-1011 RX-0213 R-1579 RG-0019
  6. The long-term technology position: UltraFan kept as an option, funded out of returns; in 2026 an UltraFan 30 demonstrator with public R&D money and a partner sought, not a launch RG-0021 RG-0029 R-0975 RX-0094 RG-0065

How it decides

  • Committees prepare, the full board decides; principal risks are allocated to committees and factored into decisions RG-0024 RG-0049 RG-0050 RG-0054
  • No vote split is public; the board answers as one voice, by consensus or majority inference RG-0030
  • Regular cadence, closer in a crisis: quarterly on cash and payments, regular updates from management in 2020 RG-0039 RG-0031
  • Precaution under uncertainty: size to the reasonable worst case, not the base case RG-0033 RG-0030
  • Debate, then public backing: once priorities are set the CEO has the board's total support; medium-term guidance goes through the board before release RG-0017 RG-0044
  • Tempo: slow to commit (distributions back 15 months after 'near term'), fast to scale returns once rated (£1bn in 2025, then £7-9bn over 2026-2028), fast to cut when cash weakens (the buyback stopped half-way in 2015) RX-0222 R-0887 RG-0042 R-0547 RG-0037 RG-0059
  • Growth in stages, shared with partners or the state: SMR on a two-stage contract with a final investment decision in 2029; UltraFan 30 as a demonstrator first, with public R&D money and a partner sought RG-0066 RG-0065
  • Before approving it needs the grid rows with and without each item, the CEO's expected scenario and predictions, the CFO's co-signature and worst column, the operating head's ready year against each EIS and support plan, both veto checks and any declared premium; a missing figure is computed from the brief and raised as a recommendation, not a veto. The CFO's co-signature is her veto check concurring with that value; a change at the revise step to a more conditional form (launch to launch if selected or hold) keeps it, and a launch or commit value that appears only at the revise step has it only if her test memo co-signed it. At confirm the game master passes the board's guidance, the ExCo package, its review, the CEO's revision and the merged orders: a revised value from the board's acceptable alternatives is approved unless the revision shows a new fact that fails a test inference RG-0044 RX-0213 RX-0296

Culture beyond the two scores

  • Capital allocation. Safety and a strong investment-grade balance sheet first; then the dividend at a 30-40% payout; then investment and extra distributions, which compete on strategic fit, value and timing. Cases above £25m are signed off by the CEO and CFO against mid-to-high-teens hurdles; gross R&D stays broadly flat. Since 2025: 9.5p for 2025 (a 32% payout), £7-9bn of buybacks over 2026-2028 (£1.4bn of the £2.5bn 2026 tranche done by July), single A from two agencies, and about £1bn on durability first. The record of cuts runs buybacks first, then the dividend, then new programme spend. In the game: one new big programme at a time, inside the envelope inference. R-0900 R-0909 RX-0248 R-0902 RX-0213 R-1579 RX-0214 R-0547 R-0597 R-0779 R-0986 RG-0059 RG-0060 RG-0068
  • Safety oversight. Since 2023 the Safety, Energy Transition & Tech Committee (chair Wendy Mars) focuses on safety and oversees technology strategy and investments; before it the Safety, Ethics and Sustainability Committee owned product and occupational safety, a moral obligation. The full board oversaw the Trent 1000 crisis; customer trust was the number-one goal in 2018; the Trent 1000 durability package (June 2025) retrofits the fleet within two years; safety is 5% of the annual bonus. No committee statement after 2020. In the game an operating-head ground is a veto ground when it fails one of his tests against the final orders (Ready by EIS for an unconditional launch or commit; No early date; Support before EIS) or his binding Civil veto still stands after the revision, even where the ExCo treated a late engine as advice; a zero-margin pass, capacity, MRO or strain advice, and a concern the revision cured lead to a recommendation, not a veto inference. RG-0049 RG-0050 RG-0025 RG-0006 RG-0027 RG-0019 RG-0068 RG-0058 R-0737
  • Shareholders and stakeholders. A UK stakeholder board: governance serves society, investors and employees. An investor (ValueAct) had a board seat in 2016-2019; payout rises were signals of the board's confidence; the 2026 AGM backed every director with about 97-99%. The UK government holds a special share that can block a takeover, with a 15% cap on any foreign holder (2022 Articles); it finances SMR (National Wealth Fund up to £599m) and is asked for UltraFan 30 R&D money; UK Export Finance backed crisis lending. In the game it has no vote of its own: the grid models no balance sheet or state stake, so it only reinforces the balance-sheet test when that test applies inference. RG-0023 RG-0005 RG-0037 RG-0047 RG-0067 RG-0066 RG-0065 R-0802
  • Pay horizon. Set by the Remuneration Committee (chair Lord Jitesh Gadhia) and the board, which used discretion in 2020 against windfall gains. Annual bonus: one-year free cash flow, underlying operating profit, margin and customer measures, with safety and people 5% each (2025: 94% of maximum for the CEO, £4.69m total pay); half deferred into shares for three years below the holding requirement. LTIP: three-year performance conditions, released two years after the period (five years in all); the plan's 2026 measures are cumulative free cash flow, average operating margin and relative TSR (FTSE 100 and S&P Global industrials), a third each, with the 2025 emissions measure dropped; that executive awards use the same measures, and that the LTIP was reinstated in May 2024, are inference (the share-plan page and a single search). The 2026 policy raised the CEO's LTIP to 750% of salary (from 375%), his bonus to 300% (from 200%), and his shareholding requirement to 750%, held two years after leaving. No measure on record pays for a programme or a technology milestone, so the long view on the widebody core comes from the board: it accepts a declared premium for the Trent 1000 upgrade within the $3B cap and for UltraFan WB within $1B, and recommends them when the widebody franchise test fails, never funding share for its own sake inference. RG-0034 RG-0035 RG-0032 RG-0050 RG-0055 RG-0056 RG-0057 RG-0058 R-0628

Ortberg and the Board (Boeing Board)

The Boeing Company Board of Directors, twelve directors under the independent chair Steve Mollenkopf, approves or vetoes every order that differs from the default: fps launches (in real life the Board approves the launch, after management's authority to offer), the 787 Re-engine, any cancel, and the 737 Rate Increase (below its real threshold but reviewed with the package); its veto binds. Its culture is scored risk aversion 4.5 of 5 and time horizon 3 of 5 (half points allowed): safety and the investment-grade rating first, proof before commitment, and a long-cycle view held back by one-to-three-year cash pay. It approves one well-founded launch more than $1B ahead of its default in the expected column that passes the buffer test and the CFO's 'Fundable when the 777X turns' test (his other views stay advice) and loses no more than $1B per item in any plausible Airbus column (half the CFO's $2B buffer); it vetoes fps via Embraer unless clearly better, a 787 Re-engine that overlaps a Solo fps by more than 2 years or loses more than $1B, a Rate Increase that loses value, meets a live problem or answers Airbus (H6), a reactive cancel (H5), and a premium above $2B inference. As CEO and the Board's only executive director, chosen by it after a search its chair led (the Board selects the CEO and has removed one, so he serves at its pleasure: inference), he reads the Board's guidance before framing and carries its would-veto list into his frame as Board risks and into his asks, not into red lines (which hold the company hard rules H1-H8 and his own red lines); he answers each recommendation in board response when deciding, and after a Board veto revises once within it, with no override against the Board (board revise: an alternative the Board named, or the default, named in board response; the Board confirms on the merged orders with its own review in hand); the Board then confirms, and a still-vetoed item reverts to the default. In Round 1 it expects his evidenced ruling on H1 and H3. Mitchill and the Board (RTX Board (P&W))

The RTX Corporation Board of Directors, chaired by Calio, with Lead Independent Director Fredric Reynolds, a retired CBS CFO; Audit is chaired by Leanne Caret since February 2024; its Finance Committee reviews significant capital appropriations, dividends, buybacks and financing. Every order that differs from hold is a Board item (GTF2 (P&W alone) launch, launch if selected or cancel; Joint Venture with Rolls-Royce commit or withdraw); its veto binds. Culture scored risk aversion 3.5 of 5 and time horizon 3 of 5 (half points allowed): the return hurdle, sole source and proof before commitment, durability first, the dividend and pre-ASR debt. It approves launch if selected readily; an unconditional launch only into a P&W selection on the record or as NGSA franchise defence with an expected edge over launch if selected of at least +$0.5B (a margin over break-even, at its 3.5); commit once Rolls-Royce's commitment is on the record or a live airframe's code includes Rolls-Royce (1, 4, 5 or 7), on its weighted value; cancel or withdraw only with a weighted value against hold of at least zero, and a cancel while a live airframe whose code includes P&W can still be served also needs the cancel row ahead of hold in every plausible column. An item below hold passes only as a declared premium of at most $0.5B that serves the assigned objective, inside the team's $1B cap (its time horizon 3). It also vetoes an item that can lose more than its own $2B against hold in a plausible column, breaks the dividend or envelope rule, carries an unresolved binding veto or red-line flag, books unrecorded upside, or is not ready by the EIS it serves inference. His test memo and veto check go to the Board with the CEO's decision; the Board reads them as its return, envelope and cancel test (each item's value against hold, the expected edge of launch over launch if selected, the cancel round and write-off, the booked number); at its 3.5 the envelope may stretch for one round only if he shows the dividend covered and debt back on its pre-ASR path. His own gate sends projects up to the Board by size; capital items reach it through the Finance Committee inference. Erginbilgic and the Board (Rolls-Royce Board)

The Rolls-Royce Holdings plc Board: 14 directors as of 1 September 2026 under the independent chair Dame Anita Frew, with George Culmer as Senior Independent Director; Erginbilgic and McCabe are its two executive directors, re-elected in April 2026. Its Safety, Energy Transition & Tech Committee (since 2023) oversees safety and technology; its Remuneration Committee set his 2026 pay (LTIP up to 750% of salary with three-year conditions, released two years later; its measures, three-year free cash flow, margin and relative TSR, come from the share-plan page and are inference for his award). Every order that differs from hold is a Board item (UltraFan narrowbody (RR alone) launch, launch if selected or cancel; Joint Venture with P&W commit or withdraw; UltraFan widebody and Trent 1000 upgrade launch or cancel); its reserved-matters schedule (December 2024) puts strategy first, but no value threshold above the CEO-CFO £25m sign-off was found, and its veto binds. Culture scored risk aversion 4 of 5 and time horizon 2.5 of 5 (half points allowed): safety, then the balance sheet; precaution sized to the reasonable worst case; a long-cycle view held behind returns first, now with single-A ratings and a £7-9bn buyback for 2026-2028; its own growth bets (UltraFan 30, SMR) are staged and shared. It approves launch if selected and a Joint Venture commit after P&W's readily; an unconditional launch only into an RR selection on the record; narrowbody items only at a non-negative weighted value with no premium; a widebody shortfall only as a declared premium within $3B, an UltraFan WB within $1B of it. It vetoes a first Joint Venture commit (commit only once P&W's commitment is on the public record or a live airframe's engine code includes P&W); overlapping programmes, including the Trent 1000 upgrade in any round where an UltraFan is in development, launched or ordered launch if selected; an item that fails Watson's maturity (Ready by EIS, for an unconditional launch or commit), early-date or support test against the final orders, or on which his binding Civil veto still stands after the revision (a zero-margin pass or capacity advice is not a veto ground); and any item that can lose more than its own bill inference. As CEO and executive director (no vote on his own package in the game, inference), he reads the Board's guidance before framing and carries its would-veto list into his red lines, answers each recommendation in board response when deciding, and after a Board veto revises once within it, with no override against the Board (board revise: an alternative the Board named, or the default); the Board then confirms, and a still-vetoed item reverts to the default. The board chose him through the open and transparent search it ran in 2022 and backs the CEO in public once it has set the priorities. McCabe and the Board (Rolls-Royce Board)

The Rolls-Royce Holdings plc Board, 14 directors as of 1 September 2026 under the independent chair Dame Anita Frew, with George Culmer, a former Lloyds CFO, as Senior Independent Director; McCabe sits on it as CFO and director, re-elected in April 2026. Its Audit Committee (chaired by Nick Luff as of the 2024 AGM script; he leaves the board at the 2027 AGM; Alessandra Genco from September 2026) covers long-term contract accounting and market and financial risk. Her pay rides on its 2026 policy (an LTIP with three-year conditions released two years later, whose measures, three-year free cash flow, margin and relative TSR, come from the share-plan page and are inference for her award; a 450% shareholding requirement). Every order that differs from hold is a Board item; its veto binds. Culture scored risk aversion 4 of 5 and time horizon 2.5 of 5 (half points allowed): safety, then the balance sheet, as in her capital frame; precaution sized to the reasonable worst case; payments only from sustainable free cash flow; with single A from two agencies and net cash, it is returning £7-9bn over 2026-2028. It vetoes any launch or commit without her co-signature, a narrowbody item whose weighted value against hold is below 0, an undeclared or capped-out widebody premium ($3B a round, $1B for an UltraFan WB), any item that can lose more than its own bill, and the Trent 1000 upgrade in any round where an UltraFan is in development, launched or ordered launch if selected inference. Her test memo and veto check go to the Board with the CEO's decision; the Board reads them as its balance-sheet, hurdle and worst-case evidence (each item's value against hold, column by column and weighted; the worst plausible column against the item's own bill; capex a year; any premium). A launch or commit without her co-signature is a Board veto ground; the Board reads her co-signature from her veto check (concur on that value), and a CEO change at the revise step to a more conditional form keeps it inference. Watson and the Board (Rolls-Royce Board)

The Rolls-Royce Holdings plc Board, 14 directors as of 1 September 2026 under the independent chair Dame Anita Frew; Watson is not a director inference. Since 2023 its Safety, Energy Transition & Tech Committee (chair Wendy Mars) focuses on safety and oversees technology strategy and investments, UltraFan included inference; Paul Adams, its ex-P&W engineer, is not on the 2026 roster (left in 2023, inference: one listing). Every order that differs from hold is a Board item; its veto binds. Culture scored risk aversion 4 of 5 and time horizon 2.5 of 5 (half points allowed): product safety its most important priority, the Trent 1000 crisis overseen directly, the risk of many new products at once; the Trent 1000 durability package (June 2025) was funded first, safety is 5% of the bonus, and the 2026 narrowbody step is an UltraFan 30 demonstrator, not a launch. It vetoes any item that fails his maturity (Ready by EIS, for an unconditional launch or commit), early-date or support test against the final orders, or on which his binding Civil veto still stands after the CEO's revision, even where the ExCo treats a late engine as advice; a zero-margin pass, capacity, MRO or strain advice, and a concern the revision cured lead to a recommendation, not a veto. It also vetoes overlapping programmes inference. His test memo and veto check go to the Board with the CEO's decision; the Board reads them as its safety and readiness evidence (each item's ready year against each live airframe's EIS, the support plan, any overlap, each concern marked as a test fail, a binding veto or a note), and a failed maturity, early-date or support test carries weight there inference. Agent file: .claude/agents/rolls-royce-watson.md

Isolation

The same hook that kept the single company agents apart in dash-2050 now covers the fifteen executive agents and the five Board agents (.claude/hooks/wargame_isolation.py). It checks every file path and command an agent uses, so it stops access by name, not a deliberately disguised one. A post-game audit of every tool call (audit.py) backs it up.

  • Own company only. Each executive and each Board has the same limits as its single company agent had. It cannot read another company's profiles, agent files or folder (/tmp/wargame-<company>). It cannot read the game master's code, the dashboard, the reports or the game master's run records. Its own company's folder stays readable: the run the game master names, plus earlier rounds' notes and orders of that run.
  • No earlier game. The earlier games' files have been moved out of the company folders into an archive no player can read. The executives are also blocked from the earlier dash-2050 run by name, so a replay cannot see its orders.
  • No engine, no game-master code. An executive or Board agent runs no game-engine command and cannot import the game master's modules. Its numbers come only from the brief that the game master writes into its company's folder.
  • Searches stay at home. Searches, wildcard reads and recursive reads must stay inside the company's own folders. The game master's scratchpad, the session transcripts and the workflow agents' transcripts are blocked.
  • Inside the company. The ExCo and its Board may read each other's agent files (they know each other), but memos, guidance and reviews pass only through the game master. Within a round, the CFO and the operating head write their tests before either sees the other's; the Board sees the ExCo's package only after the CEO has decided.
  • Tested. All 285 hook test cases behave as expected. They include 33 cases for the executive and Board agents, and 224 checks that every file each agent is told to read is allowed for that agent. All 360 tool calls the single company agents made in dash-2050 are still allowed.

Method

  1. Sources. The per-person profiles in wargame/profiles/<company>/executives/, built earlier from the companies' own earnings-call and investor-event transcripts and, for Airbus, the FY2025 Board Report. Also each team's decision rule (teams.md), the seat's role card, the company doctrine and dashboard_game.md, which maps the levers to the board.
  2. Drafting. One drafting agent per company wrote its three agent files and profiles to a fixed specification: 17 sections in a fixed order, quotes word for word with their ids, inferences labelled, and the round step each seat plays.
  3. Verification. A second agent per company re-checked every claim, id and quote against the evidence and corrected the files in place. A final pass compared the fifteen agents for consistency across companies.
  4. Independent audit. Two fresh auditors per company then read the agents again: one checked that each cited item supports its claim, the other that each agent can play its seat by the rules without leaking. A fixer re-checked every finding against the sources before changing anything. There were 165 findings; 10 were the same finding reported by both auditors. Of the other 155, the fixer made 138 changes to the agent files and rejected 4 with a reason. The 13 that belonged elsewhere are fixed in the round script, the board notes and the specification.
  5. Boards. One research agent per company searched the transcripts and filings for what they say about the board (approvals, authorisations, reserved matters, chairs' remarks) and added new items, each quote checked against its page by verify_quotes.py. It then used web search for the board's composition, rules, pay horizons, culture and past decisions. This environment blocks direct page fetches, so web facts come from search results with their URLs and are shown as search summaries, never as quotes. Each was to be corroborated by a second, differently worded search: 130 of 140 were, and the other 10 are used only as inference, never behind a score, test or veto. A separate agent then searched again: 108 items were re-searched (some corrected, none dropped); 32 were not, because the shared search budget ran out (24 of them Rolls-Royce's, whose web research came last). A drafting agent wrote the Board agent and the executives' new Board sections; a verifier checked them; a final pass calibrated the culture scores across the five boards.
  6. Page review. Two more reviewers read this page: one recomputed its numbers and quotes from the data, the other read it on desktop and phone. Their 32 findings, including gaps in the isolation, are fixed.
  7. Mechanical check. check_agents.py checks each agent's front matter and section order, and that every cited id exists. It checks every signature quote (each agent's voice lines and the quotes on its card) word for word against its source item, with "..." marking any gap, and that each card quote's date and perspective match the source.
  8. Limits. Airbus's agents rest on what the Board Report says about them, not on their speech. Four records are thin and Airbus's three are filing-based; those agents defer instead of inventing. Volume is not trust: Watson's 27 items come almost all from one day, and the profiles' own confidence ratings are shown next to the volume. The "as voiced in dash-2050" lines are the earlier single company agent's role-play, shown for comparison, not evidence. The Boards' own words are few and mostly old, and their dollar thresholds are the ExCo's game parameters adopted by inference. How the agents behave in play is untested until the game is run.
